title: What's New: Moving Tables and Fields Between AppSource Extensions (2025 release wave 1)

chapters.title: How Moving Tables and Fields Works
What Can Be Moved - Tables and Fields
Pre-submission best practices and local validation setup
Performance characteristics of moves and summary

features.name: Move Tables and Fields Between Extensions
features.description: Ability for AL developers to move tables and fields between extensions without writing upgrade code. Supported for AppSource extensions targeting runtime version 150 and higher, and for on-premise extensions for Business Central version 26.0 and higher. Per-tenant extensions are not supported.
caveats: Per-tenant extensions not supported
Only minimal breaking changes when moving to extensions with no dependency relationship
Not efficient for moving all tables
Schema must remain the same except non-breaking changes like adding fields

features.name: Obsolation Property with Pending Move State
features.description: Use the ObsoleteState property set to 'pending move' to mark a table or field as unavailable in a future version. Must be paired with MoveTo property containing the destination app ID. When published, they become unavailable until a destination extension takes ownership.
caveats: MoveTo property must contain exact destination app ID
Table definition must be kept in source extension for validation
Blocking validation prevents takeover if source is moving to a different destination
New tables and fields created if source extension not published

features.name: MoveTo and MoveFrom Properties
features.description: Source extension uses MoveTo property with destination app ID. Destination extension uses MoveFrom property with source extension app ID. Both must match for successful move validation.
caveats: App IDs must match between source and destination
Destination must have same schema as source except for non-breaking changes

features.name: Move Down Scenario
features.description: Moving tables from a source extension to dependency extensions. The destination is a dependency of the source. Use case is splitting a monolithic app into smaller parts with different teams or extracting common functionality.

features.name: Move Up Scenario
features.description: Moving tables up to extensions that depend on the source extension. The destination extensions depend on the source. Use case is splitting country-specific functionality into separate localized apps.

features.name: Lateral Move Scenario
features.description: Moving tables between extensions with no dependency relationship between source and destination. This is a breaking change as there is no dependency relationship to maintain relationships between symbols.
caveats: Lateral moves are breaking changes
No dependency relationship to maintain symbol relationships

features.name: Field Movement Constraints
features.description: Fields can be moved from a base table to a table extension with the same base table, or from a table extension to another table extension with the same base table. Moving from table extension back to base table (consolidation) is not supported.
caveats: Consolidation (moving from table extension back to base table) not supported
Both extensions must have same target table

features.name: Propagate Dependencies Property
features.description: Set propagate dependencies property to true in the monolith app version where moves occur or when moving objects down to direct dependencies in non-breaking scenarios. This ensures apps depending on the monolith continue to have access to moved tables after the new version, and allows removing objects from source and redefining them in destination without obsoletion.
caveats: Only applies to downward moves to direct dependencies
Breaking change if moving up or laterally

features.name: Movement Happens During Sync Stage
features.description: Moves occur during the syncing stage of an extension lifecycle, which is after publishing and before installation. This is when the database schema is changed to enable the move.
caveats: Source extension must be deployed before destination for takeover to work

features.name: VS Code Deployment for Development Testing
features.description: Developers can test table and field moves using Visual Studio Code development environment. Business Central handles deployment when customers install AppSource extensions.

features.name: Reusing Existing Extensions as Move Destinations
features.description: New extensions do not need to be created to move tables and fields. Existing extensions can be used as destinations by publishing new versions.

features.name: Takeover Validation - Single Destination Only
features.description: A destination extension can only take over a table or field if it is the exact destination declared in the source extension. Validation prevents multiple extensions from taking over the same moved object.
caveats: Only the declared destination can take over a moved table or field

features.name: Fallback to New Table Creation if Source Not Published
features.description: If the source extension of a move is not published on the system, new tables or fields will be created for the destination extension instead of performing a move.

features.name: Moving Dependent Objects and Dependencies
features.description: When moving tables and fields, dependent objects like reports and pages can move with them. Dependencies must be handled through common dependencies or propagation mechanisms.

features.name: AppSource move validation
features.description: AppSource submission process includes automatic validation for table and field moves, checking source extension existence, compilation, schema changes, and preventing invalid takeovers. Source extension must be submitted first unless destination is library extension.
caveats: Source extension must be submitted first unless destination is library extension
Both extensions must compile after move

features.name: Local move validation through AppSource scope analyzer
features.description: Enable move validation rules locally using AppSource scope analyzer by building source extension, enabling analyzer, creating directory, and setting new property to point to source directory.
caveats: Requires AL-GO or development environment setup

features.name: Table and field move performance optimization
features.description: Moving tables and fields is designed for large data volumes with minimal copying. Field moves between extensions use column rename, field moves from base to extension use AL data transfer, and table moves use database rename.
caveats: Field moves from base table to extension require data transfer
No performance comparison provided for non-table scenarios
